topic: What Lenders Look for in Bank Statements
objective: Explain what lenders scan for when reviewing business bank statements.

slides.subheadline: Your statements tell a story — make sure it's clear.

slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: Bank statements give lenders a real-time view of how your business actually trades — consistency of income, how you manage outgoings, and whether there are signs of financial stress like dishonours or frequent overdrawn balances. Several months of clean statements can strengthen an application.

slides.headline: Key things to know
bullet_points: Most lenders ask for three to six months of statements
Multiple accounts may all need to be provided
Unusual one-off transactions are worth explaining upfront
Statements are often assessed alongside other financials

caption:
Bank statements are one of the most revealing documents in a loan application — they show, in real time, how the business actually operates rather than how it looks on paper. Lenders are typically scanning for consistency, signs of financial stress, and how existing commitments are being managed.

It's worth reviewing your own statements before applying, so you can explain any unusual activity upfront rather than leaving a lender to guess.
